display.title: Episode 446: The Shpoler Zeide and the Strange Pillar of Fire (Vov Tishrei)
display.summary_short: On Vov Tishrei, the Shpoler Zeide's yahrzeit, Uncle Yossi tells of the Alter Rebbe's holy book that rose to heaven in a pillar of fire, and remembers Rebbetzin Chana.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Vov Tishrei 5751, between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. Uncle Yossi marks the yahrzeit of the Shpoler Zeide, Rabbi Aryeh Leib, and the weekly march is the 'Hop Kozak', a tune attributed to the Shpoler Zeide himself. Two sisters from a Brooklyn girls' school recite the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: 'The Strange Pillar of Fire'. Chassidim fighting a fire at the Alter Rebbe's home see a winding pillar of flame rise into the sky. The story explains: the Shpoler Zeide once read a book the Alter Rebbe was writing, 'Sefer shel Tzaddikim', and begged that it be returned to heaven, foretelling that it would rise in a pillar of fire like Eliyahu HaNavi, and wishing that his own soul would rise the same way. At the moment the book burned, the Shpoler Zeide passed away. Uncle Yossi then remembers Rebbetzin Chana, the Rebbe's mother, whose yahrzeit is also Vov Tishrei, and who made ink from plants so her husband could keep writing Torah in exile. The show ends with a talk on the Ten Days of Teshuvah and Yom Kippur.
display.lesson: Remember tzaddikim on their yahrzeit and follow their example; teshuvah brings us back close to Hashem.

date.note: 'Today is Vov Tishrei', a few days after Rosh Hashanah, and Yom Kippur falls on 'this coming Shabbos' (10 Tishrei 5751 = 1990-09-29).

advisories.note: The Shpoler Zeide passes away at the end of the story.
Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson imprisoned in Soviet Russia for teaching Torah.

privacy.note: Two Shema guests named in full.
